title: India may go duty-free, but is weak in 10 of EU’s top 20 garments
summary:

title: China lost 53% of US apparel sales, but sold rivals $8.5 bn in fabric

title: UK to launch joint export finance scheme for SMEs in 2027

title: US textile coalition unveils $29 bn sourcing incentive proposal
summary:
NCTO, AAFA, USFIA and USINFI jointly filed their first-ever Section 301 proposal, marking a rare US textile-apparel policy alliance. 
The plan targets $29 billion in Western Hemisphere textile exports and 56,000 US jobs through regional sourcing. 
A 20 per cent base credit plus US yarn/fabric incentives could reshape USMCA and CAFTA-DR sourcing if USTR approves it.

title: Hong Kong's trade with Gulf Arab countries rises 35% in 5 months
summary:
Hong Kong’s trade with Gulf Arab countries rose over 35 per cent in the first five months of 2026, against 5 per cent annual growth in 2025.
Trade with the United Arab Emirates climbed over 52 per cent, signalling stronger Asia-Gulf flows.
The corridor is relevant for textile and apparel exporters, importers and sourcing teams alongside Gulf wealth funds’ 40 per cent Asia allocation.

title: Germany’s leading economic index strengthens in May 2026: TCB
summary:
Germany’s LEI rose 0.6 per cent in May 2026 to 87.5, following an upwardly revised 0.1 per cent gain in April, signalling a firmer near-term business-cycle reading. 
The six-month LEI trend stayed negative, down 1.1 per cent from November 2025 to May 2026. 
The CEI edged up 0.1 per cent to 103.3, but its six-month performance remained marginally negative.

title: Netherlands goods exports rise 5.5% in May 2026
summary:
Netherlands' working-day-adjusted goods export volume rose 5.5 per cent year on year in May 2026, after 4.6 per cent in April. 
Petroleum products and electrical machinery drove exports, indicating firmer European goods flows for trade and sourcing teams. 
Imports rose 5.4 per cent on petroleum products, machinery and chemicals. 
CBS said better conditions need not mean faster export growth.

title: Source Fashion concludes, boosting UK manufacturing at Excel London
summary:
Source Fashion recorded its strongest edition yet after relocating to Excel London, attracting over 305 exhibitors from 19 countries and a 20 per cent rise in high-value buyers.
The event highlighted growing demand for resilient sourcing, stronger UK manufacturing capabilities and long-term global supplier partnerships, while setting the stage for further expansion in January 2027.

title: US T&A import volume declines 7% in January-May 2026
summary:
US textile and apparel import volumes fell 7.28 per cent year on year to 37.97 billion SME during January-May 2026, led by declines in apparel, textile, cotton, and man-made fibre imports.
Exports also dropped 7.13 per cent to 838.09 million kg, as weaker yarn and fabric shipments outweighed growth in apparel exports, reflecting softer global demand and trade activity.

title: India-EU FTA: 63% cotton basket could cap apparel export gains
summary:
India’s FTA with the EU can improve price competitiveness, but tariffs alone will not double apparel exports.
TexPro data show India’s Europe-bound basket remains heavily cotton-focused, while demand is stronger for jerseys and outerwear.
The biggest opportunity lies in expanding MMF capacity and higher-value product categories before the agreement takes effect.

title: Sri Lanka’s apparel recovery: Is Washington holding the thread?
summary:
Sri Lanka’s apparel exports rose 7.96 per cent in May 2026, driven by a 15.36 per cent jump in US shipments, highlighting its reliance on American demand. 
However, the recovery faces a key test as the country seeks a trade deal before July 24 to avoid a proposed 12.5 per cent US tariff that could weaken its competitiveness against rival exporters.

title: Why is Bangladesh’s apparel industry shedding jobs?
summary:
Bangladesh’s garment sector is reportedly facing factory closures and layoffs, leaving thousands jobless. 
Many workers, 20,000 as per some estimates, were reportedly affected in the first half of the year amid falling orders, rising costs and financing challenges facing the industry. 
The crisis underscores the sector’s struggle to balance global competitiveness with employment stability.

title: Jordan's apparel exports climb to $751 mn in January-April 2026
summary:
Jordan's apparel exports rose to 533.78 million JD in January–April 2026 from 518.86 million JD a year earlier, supported by strong shipments of knitted garments.
Total textile and apparel exports also climbed to 582.26 million JD, while apparel and overall textile imports recorded modest increases, reflecting resilient trade activity and sustained global demand for Jordanian products.

title: Can Bangladesh hold on to its EU edge after LDC graduation?
summary:
Bangladesh is reportedly simultaneously pursuing an EU free trade agreement and GSP Plus status to protect its exports as duty-free access ends after LDC graduation. 
With the EU buying nearly half its exports, delays in an FTA and stronger competition from India and Vietnam, stakeholders believe, could erode the country’s hard-won edge in its biggest market.

title: Amazon-AEPC’s $80 bn goal rewires India’s apparel exports
summary:
Amazon's $80 bn export goal arrives as US tariff changes weaken China’s direct-to-consumer advantage, giving Indian apparel MSMEs a rare opportunity to expand through marketplace exports.  
The opportunity may be short-lived. Section 122 expiry and ongoing US legal challenges could quickly alter India’s tariff advantage, making faster exporter onboarding and pricing discipline critical.

title: India amends footwear QCOs to ease compliance
summary:
India has amended two footwear Quality Control Orders for leather, rubber, polymeric and other footwear and components.
The legacy stock clearance deadline moves to July 31, 2027, giving manufacturers, distributors and retailers more time to liquidate inventory.
Footwear makers may import up to 4,500 sample pairs annually for R&D, subject to non-sale and record rules.

title: India exports $177 mn; may make 90% of luxury embroidery—no credit
summary:
India’s embroidery exports are expanding rapidly, with over one-third shipped to Italy and France, underscoring its key role in luxury fashion supply chains.
Yet customs origin rules often credit only the final manufacturing country.
As traceability evolves, recognising craftsmanship alongside manufacturing could become a new source of value in global fashion.

title: Why did 830 Italian leather firms close while luxury prices stay high?
summary:
Italy’s apparel exports continue to grow, but Florence’s fashion manufacturing base is shrinking as workshops close and skilled jobs disappear.
The gap highlights how rising export values do not necessarily sustain suppliers.
Long-term competitiveness depends on ensuring more value reaches manufacturers, protecting specialist skills and strengthening resilient local production.

title: US T&A imports drop to $39 bn in Jan-May; Vietnam retains top spot
summary:
US textile and apparel imports fell 8.92 per cent to $39.13 billion in January-May 2026, according to the Office of Textiles and Apparel (OTEXA).
Vietnam remained the top supplier, while China's shipments declined sharply.
Apparel and non-apparel imports both weakened, reflecting shifting sourcing towards Southeast Asia amid tariff concerns and changing supply chain strategies.
